maria (PM): Quick thread 1: Need to pick a burst-shaping approach for the Dedicated GA pilots. Two customer asks: guaranteed 2x short bursts (10m) and predictable billing for burst usage. We have three options below. Need engineering + billing + legal thumbs by Tue.
kevin (Eng): TL;DR list the three options, tradeoffs. I can prototype pool configs if we agree.
maria (PM): Options (brief):
A) Hard-reserve "burst band" per tenant: pre-allocate extra slots that are billable at premium. Predictable, simple, higher cost.
B) Soft-burst with credit bucket: customers earn burst credits -> consume; infra preempts non-reserved workloads during bursts. More complex billing but cheaper.
C) On-demand spill -> fall back to hosted model during spikes; lowest infra change but breaks private isolation guarantees.
jen (Sales): Customers will pay for A for GA. B might be attractive for SMB tiers. C is non-starter for customers who require private-only traffic.
alex (SRE): Ops notes: A requires enforcement and a deterministic preemption policy. We need fast eviction (<200ms) and clear observability. B requires tenant credit accounting + predictive prewarm; potential cascading if many use credits simultaneously. C risks data path routing complexity.
tom (Billing): Billing impact: A = separate SKU line (burst units, per-minute). B = credit accounting + monthly carryover policy (spec). Both need legal-approved contract language. C = no billing change but SLA downgrade.
maya (Legal): I'll draft SOW language for A and B templates. B needs clear definitions for "credit expiration" and "preemption events". We should avoid ambiguous terms.
sasha (ML): Performance note: For embedding-heavy bursts, switching to a quantized model variant during bursts can reduce required GPU footprint by ~30% and increase packing. But we must measure quality delta. Could be part of B or A as opt-in.
kevin (Eng): Implementation effort estimates: A: ~3 dev-days to add policy layer + 1 SRE day to onboard pilots. B: ~2 sprints (billing + infra + tests). C: <1 week but requires routing change and a clear opt-in flag.
maria (PM): Proposed GA path: ship A for pilot customers who need predictability, run B as opt-in experiment for cost-conscious customers. Roll B into GA after 2 pilot cycles. Does that sound reasonable?
alex (SRE): Agree. For A, we need preemption rules. Proposal: preempt by FIFO across non-reserved tasks, backoff 30s, with per-pod grace of 5s. Also add these metrics: reserved_util, burst_evictions, spillover_latency.
kevin (Eng): Suggest a minimal config format for A: ```
reserved_pool: {
  tenant_id: "acme",
  base_units: 80,
  burst_band: 160, // 2x
  burst_window_minutes: 10,
  preemptible_policy: "strict"
}
```
jenn (typo) -- jen (Sales): Put a note that customers want a UI toggle for burst opt-in + preview of cost before enabling. UX request.
maya (Legal): Also require an audit log entry whenever preemption fires for compliance.
kevin (Eng): Good call. We'll emit preempt events to event-stream. Also will add a flag: `burst.force_override` for oncall.
sasha (ML): I'll produce quantized vs baseline eval: throughput, median latency, and embedding cosine drift. ETA 48h.
alex (SRE): I'll write the runbook skeleton: steps to detect overload, steps to trigger spillover, how to roll back pool config. Will link PR.
maria (PM): Action items: kevin prototype config + sim (EOD Wed), alex runbook draft (Thu AM), sasha quant eval (Fri), tom + maya draft billing + SOW language (Thu). Sales to confirm pilot acceptance. Meet Fri 11 to finalize.
deploy-bot: Created ticket RDW-6120 "GA burst-shaping: hard-reserve + billing template" -> https://tracker.example/RDW-6120 :robot_face: 
kevin (Eng): queued load sim: `./tools/sim_burst --tenants acme,beta --pattern 2x-10m --concurrency 50` results to s3://rdw-sims/1759993333/
alex (SRE): adding dashboards: grafana panel reserved_util and burst_evictions, alert if spillover > 5% for 5m.
maria (PM): Thanks. If any blockers, DM me.
